comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C22, C94-C97. Both evaluations find the electrophysiological measurements of wild-type and mutant channel inactivation kinetics to be well-supported with quantitative data. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer review also rates as SUPPORTED.

Strong disagreement on claims C65-C70. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the 'deep resting state' model is speculative without direct experimental validation. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, with reviewers stating 'None of the explanations are consistent with the data shown' regarding the mechanistic model for pore lipids and inactivation.

Agreement on claims C23-C24. Both evaluations accept the SDS-PAGE observations and inferences about PTMs and binding partners as reasonable, though OpenEval notes these are not definitively established without additional characterization. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Agreement on claims C3, C4, C42-C44. Both evaluations accept the structural observations of MDFIC binding and induced conformational changes. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with note that C44 requires further validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, stating the structural data is not disputed.

Major disagreement on claims C5, C54-C60, C83. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the high-resolution cryo-EM data clearly shows lipid density and interactions. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN with significant concerns, stating 'the major conclusions and central tenets of the paper, especially a role for pore lipids in inactivation, lack data to support them' and questioning the lipid fitting to cryo-EM density.

Partial disagreement on claims C7-C9, C51-C53, C62. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, accepting both structural observations and mechanistic inferences. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, accepting the structural data but questioning the mechanistic interpretation linking structural changes to the broken lipid-R2456 interaction and inactivation mechanism.

Disagreement on claims C63-C64. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the comparison with mPIEZO1 structures and cited data provide reasonable support. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, criticizing lack of proper referencing and discussion: 'the literature on this point is still not at all referenced or discussed.'

Disagreement on claims C12-C13. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as established findings from cited literature. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, criticizing that 'the literature on this point is still not at all referenced or discussed' and lacks proper quantitative comparison in the manuscript.

Agreement on claims C2, C30-C34. Both evaluations accept the quantitative structural measurements from cryo-EM data. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED including claims C35-C37. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED for the structural observations, acknowledging this is the first human PIEZO1 structure.

Agreement on claims C1, C10-C11, C71, C73-C75, C77-C78, C80. Both evaluations accept this background information from established literature. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED but notes 'There is little to no attempt to improve the referencing' and suggests presentation could be enhanced.

Agreement on uncertainty for claims C84-C87. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the curvature-inactivation links are not strongly established. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, noting authors have weakened their claims but evidence remains incomplete for the relationship between structural features and functional outcomes.

Disagreement on claims C45, C98. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the electrophysiological data and structural evidence support the claims. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, repeatedly requesting quantification: 'No quantification is provided' and 'it is still missing quantification from the human mutant + MDFIC data.'

Agreement on claims C25-C27. Both evaluations accept the cryo-EM data collection, processing, and structural observations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for C25-C29. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED for the structural data quality and resolution, though interpretation of specific features is questioned separately.

Agreement on claims C15-C21. Both evaluations accept this clinical and population genetics background from prior research. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, noting this established literature is not disputed.

Agreement on claims C38, C46. Both evaluations accept the inference that MDFIC improves structural stability of mutants based on improved resolution. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, finding this consistent with the data showing better resolution for mutant-MDFIC complexes.

Disagreement on claim C29. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the inference about auxiliary subunits/cytosolic plug reasonable based on density features and SDS-PAGE. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, stating 'There is not even any extra discussion provided on this point' and noting lack of characterization.

Major disagreement on claims C6, C61-C62, C83, C89. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding convergent evidence from structure, functional studies, and mutant analysis supports the proposed role of pore lipids in inactivation. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN with significant concerns about the central claim regarding pore lipids in inactivation, stating conclusions 'lack data to support them.'

OpenEval found claims C99-C103 regarding quantitative structural measurements of MDFIC effects on wild-type versus mutant channels to be SUPPORTED by cryo-EM data comparisons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific comparative measurements.

OpenEval found claims C14, C72, C81 regarding MDFIC's role and prior research (Zhou et al., 2023) to be SUPPORTED as established background context. Peer review addresses these claims within R15 as part of broader background literature but does not evaluate them separately.

OpenEval found claims C90-C93 regarding functional data and future applications to be SUPPORTED, noting C92-C93 are aspirational statements about potential applications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these forward-looking claims.
